heuristic.applicability: Prefer at the nominal calibrated cabinet location when drawer progress, finger state, TCP/object relations and motion cues are reliable but the high-level switch may land before/after release or before/after red contact. This model avoids moving all targets with a possibly noisy drawer frame and can exploit the observed red-Y variation directly.

handoff.entry_conditions: Nominal drawer calibration; any causally recognizable demonstrated phase from closed/high/free through open/front-release/red approach. Observed state must be physically coherent; phase prediction is not an entry proof.
handoff.exit_conditions: Drawer_position safely above strict 0.26 m, near-zero drawer motion, front relinquished, and red closed upon with observable TCP/red upward co-motion for nominal handoff.
handoff.failure_signatures: Stage oscillation or actions inconsistent with drawer progress/finger state, drawer below threshold after pull, continued front drag after opening, TCP/red misalignment, closure without red co-motion, drop during lift, or IK nonconvergence. Such signatures are monitoring cues, not demonstrated recovery capabilities.
handoff.overlap_role: All actions 0:470 are retained. The phase labels include release/retreat, red approach, closure and lift within the full 230:470 action-supervised overlap shared with red_transfer in every trajectory.
handoff.successor_readiness: An early switch is supported after drawer opening/red exposure at 230; the nominal robust switch is after the close/lift phase when red and TCP co-move near 470.

heuristic.limitations: World targets can fail under drawer/cabinet displacement; drawer_frame_tracking covers that failure. Index-derived phase labels describe successful nominal occurrences and may not classify unseen failure/recovery states. The auxiliary classifier does not observe contact truth, does not gate execution by itself, and cannot prove grasp. The 12 demonstrations have nearly identical drawer timing, a single cabinet calibration and no failed pulls or drops. Absolute poses can be unreachable from changed configurations; shared IK reports this. tcp_increment_servo is the alternative for local configuration deviation.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: No caller arguments are required; all intent is the fixed open_drawer responsibility and all inputs are causal observations. The high-level agent may invoke at any represented nominal phase but must monitor physical cues rather than trust a predicted phase as contact proof. Use drawer_frame_tracking for a known shifted drawer anchor and tcp_increment_servo for modest off-path TCP/tracking perturbations. The standard U-Net backbone and H2/16/8 timing stay unchanged; only a trainable causal condition encoder and training-only auxiliary classifier are added and saved with the model/EMA.
heuristic.rationale: Observed evidence: nominal execution changes responsibility several times despite one continuous segment: high free-space handle approach (0-140), gripper closure and articulated pull (about 145-230), opening/release and retreat (230-300), reorientation and red-relative approach/descent (320-445), then closure and lift (445-470). Drawer position, finger width/velocity, TCP-to-drawer geometry, TCP-to-red geometry and red/TCP co-motion are causal observable cues. Demo1001 and demo1005 show red-dependent Y differences after 320 while drawer timing remains nearly identical. Deployment can enter at an intermediate state, making stage confusion a likely failure. This policy uses world position plus 6D world rotation and gripper as its action, but a registered per-frame MLP encodes relational causal features for the unchanged diffusion backbone. A registered five-class auxiliary head predicts the supervised occurrence phase (approach, pull, release/retreat, red approach, red close/lift) from the same causal condition. Masked cross-entropy at weight 0.05 supplies a real gradient through the condition encoder in addition to diffusion loss; the label is never an inference input. Expected benefit, not established recovery: sharper conditioning on observable stage when invoked mid-segment.
heuristic.statement: Phase-supervised relational conditioning with world Cartesian pose targets

assignment.subgoal: Primary responsibility: acquire the drawer front, pull the drawer from closed to a reliably open state, release/retract from the drawer, and continue through the demonstrated handoff until the red block is grasped and beginning to lift. Observed contact/motion: the gripper approaches low over the drawer front, closes, pulls mainly along world -X, then opens and retreats upward before moving above and descending to the exposed red block; gripper/object co-motion is used only as an observable contact cue because contact truth is unavailable. Entry is a closed drawer (drawer_position about 0), open gripper, high TCP, red inside the drawer, and blue outside. At the nominal exit observation 470, drawer_position is 0.300, fingers are about 0.018 m, and red is grasped and lifted to z about 0.093-0.107 m while blue is unchanged. Examples: demo1000 observations 230/280 show the fully opened drawer followed by release/vertical retreat; 400/445/470 show red alignment, closure, and lift. The front images at demo1000 indices 150, 230, and 445 support the drawer-pull, open-drawer, and red-contact interpretation. Purpose/expected benefit: the retained post-opening transition should let the red-transfer successor accept a switch before or after drawer release and red contact; it is not evidence of recovery from unseen failed pulls or misgrasps.

conversion_check.description: World position/6D rotation labels reconstruct each demonstrated commanded TCP pose; shared IK is independently checked by FK position/rotation and unchanged gripper scalar. Gram-Schmidt projects only sampled non-orthogonal values.

contract.cut_relation: All actions in every assigned [0,470) segment are action-supervised. Auxiliary phase labels partition but do not trim the cut. Actions 230:470 remain full overlap with red_transfer across front release, retreat, red approach, closure and lift.
contract.output_semantics: Each slot is an absolute world-frame TCP target: world position [3] in metres, world rotation as the first two matrix columns [6], and native gripper scalar [1]. Prediction slots are t-1..t+14 and execution uses slots 1..8 for t..t+7. Sampled 6D rotation is projected by Gram-Schmidt. The target is passed to panda_kinematics.solve_ik from fresh measured qpos, and the gripper scalar is appended unchanged for common sign-based execution. The phase label/head does not enter decode_action.
contract.parameter_semantics: No caller parameters. The policy's fixed intent is the assigned open_drawer responsibility. Two causal observations determine relational condition and the training-only phase prediction; the initial observation is duplicated only by the framework at episode start.
